title: EFC — Master Specification (v1 Archive)
description: Canonical master specification for Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC), defining the formal structure and baseline equations for three tightly coupled layers: EFC-S (structural/halo), EFC-D (energy-flow dynamics), and EFC-C0 (entropy–information capacity mapping). The paper fixes notation, establishes the central energy-flow potential Ef = ρ(1−S), and provides the compact mathematical core that all higher-level EFC models, simulations, and epistemic layers reference.

energy_flow_potential.description: Local energy-flow potential coupling mass density ρ and dimensionless entropy S into a single field. High density with low entropy yields large Ef; high entropy suppresses Ef even for dense regions.

low_entropy_anchor.description: Definition of a low-entropy anchor: a region A where the coarse-grained entropy density is much lower than the background, serving as a seed for halo formation.

halo_mass_profile.description: Parameterised radial mass density profile for a halo with central density ρ₀ and mass scale radius rₛ.

halo_entropy_profile.description: Parameterised radial entropy profile for a halo with entropy floor S₀ and entropy core radius rᶜ.

mass_density.description: Standard mass density definition used in EFC-D as a baseline quantity.

information_capacity.description: EFC-C0 baseline relation mapping entropy to information capacity at fixed density.

key_results.main_finding: EFC is formally specified as a three-layer thermodynamic-information framework (EFC-S, EFC-D, EFC-C0) that derives gravitational dynamics, halo structure, and expansion history from a single energy-flow potential Ef = ρ(1−S) without invoking dark matter or dark energy.

kill_criteria: KC1: If the energy-flow potential Ef = ρ(1−S) is shown to be fundamentally incompatible with observed galactic rotation curves across multiple morphological types after proper calibration of halo parameters.
KC2: If entropy-structured halo profiles (joint ρh, Sh) cannot reproduce the mass–concentration relation observed in gravitational lensing surveys.
KC3: If the EFC-derived effective expansion history H(z) cannot be brought into agreement with BAO and Type Ia supernovae distance-redshift data for any physically motivated entropy evolution.
KC4: If low-entropy anchors as defined by ⟨s⟩_A ≪ ⟨s⟩_background are shown not to correlate with observed sites of structure formation in large-scale surveys.
KC5: If the information-capacity relation I(S) ∝ (1−S) leads to predictions contradicted by black-hole thermodynamics or holographic entropy bounds.
